title: Building a --snapshot disk changes the permissions of the caller's own files
details:
`BuildExt4Dir` runs `find "$FC_DIR" ! -readable -exec chmod u+rX {} +` over its source directory before `mke2fs -d` reads it (`internal/fcdisk/fcdisk.go:143`). The pre-pass was added for image stores, which carry the mode-0000 `/etc/gshadow` that every distro base image ships, and which would otherwise stop the build dead.

`buildSnapshotDisks` passes the user's own host path as that directory (`internal/engine/firecracker.go:601`). So `--snapshot`, documented as a read-only point-in-time copy of a host directory, edits the source it claims only to read.

fakeroot does not contain the change. It records the intended mode in its own database and still issues a real `chmod`, which lands on disk. Measured directly: a file created 0000, passed through `fakeroot -- bash -c 'find <dir> ! -readable -exec chmod u+rX {} +'`, comes back 0600.

Reproduce it with `chmod 000 ~/keys/secret`, then `cs-sandbox create x --engine firecracker --snapshot ~/keys`, then `stat -c %a ~/keys/secret`. The image-store path already unpacks into a temp tree first (`internal/fcdisk/cache.go`), which is where the pre-pass belongs for a snapshot too.
